title: The “API Contract”: Checkpoints
use_cases: Use when defining long-term narrative targets to prevent model drift
Implement when managing complex information asymmetry between characters
Configure when specific pacing or attention allocation is required for an arc
Use when setting strict logical boundaries and plot restrictions for generation
content:
The most important concept in our pipeline is the Checkpoint.

A Checkpoint is a target state defined by the author (often ~20 chapters ahead). Instead of asking the model to write linearly and hope it lands well, we ask it to generate a path that lands precisely on a target state.

A Checkpoint includes:

- Outcome (non-negotiable): e.g., “The hero must lose the tournament.”
- Knowledge Map: who knows what by the end of the arc. e.g. “By Chapter 20, Alice knows Bob is the traitor, but Bob must NOT know that Alice knows.”
- Narrative Weight Distribution: where to spend attention. e.g. “Give ~70% focus to the antagonist’s backstory.”
- Constraints / Forbidden Moves: hard boundaries. e.g. “Do not reveal the killer’s motive yet.”
